projects.name: PersonalPitcher
projects.description: The site you are reading this on. A personal AI pitch platform: visitors ask questions in natural language and get answers generated from curated profile data, with the real request pipeline rendered live beneath each answer rather than hidden.
highlights: Intent-routed retrieval over curated Markdown/JSON profile data (no vector store — routing, not embeddings)
Four-tier provider fallback: a self-hosted model on a Mac on the home LAN, then OpenAI, then a local Ollama, then a regex classifier as last resort
Two independent circuit breakers, so a laptop that is asleep or away cannot consume the paid provider's failure budget, and a struggling paid provider cannot lock out the free local one
A short reachability probe in front of the LAN tier: an absent host drops packets rather than refusing them, so without it every request would stall on TCP retries for roughly twenty seconds
Breakers trip only on transient failures, and are shared between answer generation and intent classification so a failing tier is not probed twice per request
Token streaming over SSE, with the request's real workflow trail streamed alongside the answer and rendered in the UI
Waiting state that reports which tier is actually serving — including saying so when the home machine is asleep — with a live elapsed clock during cold model loads
Guardrails keeping answers grounded in curated profile data, plus per-IP rate limiting, a separate daily question quota, and request validation
Structured JSON request logging with per-request workflow steps and daily rotation, plus throttled push alerts for exceptional events such as a tier going down or recovering
Deployed via multi-stage Docker build using Next.js standalone output
Clean portfolio UI
AI-powered answers
Clean portfolio UI including a hero section, photo cards, and Q&A timeline
